key_insight: A self-supervised foundation model trained on overnight pulse oximetry can extract rich physiological signatures that go beyond heart rate and oxygen saturation, improving health and risk prediction.
clinical_relevance: This could enable non-invasive screening and longitudinal monitoring of cardiometabolic risk and other health states from routine sleep recordings, potentially supporting precision medicine.
method: Trained PulseOx-FM on 6,995,558 pulse oximetry segments from 42,282 overnight recordings in 10,704 participants.
Used self-supervised learning to learn representations from raw PPG/pulse oximetry waveforms.
Evaluated against age prediction, external out-of-distribution generalization, and multiple phenotypic and prospective outcomes.
evidence_signal: The model outperformed existing open-source and proprietary feature extractors on chronological age, generalized to an external cohort, predicted 64 phenotypic targets, and identified two-year hypertension incidence in normotensive individuals.
watch_item: Because the results come from overnight sleep-monitoring data, real-world deployment will need careful validation across devices, populations, and clinical settings before use as a decision tool.
paper_title: A foundation model of wearable pulse oximetry reveals physiological signatures of health and cardiometabolic risk
